body:
I think I have the same issue (or it's very closely related) on my work code base. The smallest fragment I could come up with is this:

```python
if False:
    # fmt: off # some other comment
    pass
```

Putting the `fmt: off` comment at the top level does not trigger the issue. It needs to be in a block.

The code above then results in the following diff output:

```diff
Mode(target_versions={<TargetVersion.PY310: 10>}, line_length=120, string_normalization=False, is_pyi=False, is_ipynb=False, skip_source_first_line=False, magic_trailing_comma=True, python_cell_magics=set(), preview=False, unstable=False, enabled_features=set())
--- source
+++ first pass
@@ -1,3 +1,3 @@
 if False:
-    # fmt: off # some other comment
+            # fmt: off # some other comment
     pass
--- first pass
+++ second pass
@@ -1,3 +1,3 @@
 if False:
-            # fmt: off # some other comment
+                # fmt: off # some other comment
     pass
```

HTH

After a quick bisect (thanks to the black team for having such a clean history, **much** appreciated 🙏), I end up with commit b895a73fd4997657a80f2f3f2785c5d496739f6e as the culprit. Unsurprisingly, this commit deals with `fmt: on/off` pragmas 😅

The original issue: #1245.

issue.title: Fix crash and instability with nested fmt directives in comment
issue.body:
*   Fix `BracketTracker.mark` to ensure `bracket_depth` is set on all leaves, even when matching opening brackets are missing on the current line. This prevents an `AttributeError` in `is_line_short_enough` when processing lines containing only closing brackets.
*   Update `src/black/comments.py` and `src/black/linegen.py` to use `_contains_fmt_directive` instead of strict `in` checks for `FMT_OFF`/`FMT_ON`. This ensures that nested or complex comment blocks (like `# # fmt: off`) are correctly identified as `STANDALONE_COMMENT` blocks with special handling, avoiding incorrect splitting or unstable formatting.
*   Added regression tests in `tests/test_fmt_off_on_comments.py`.

### 🛠️ Fix crash and instability with nested `fmt` directives in comments

This PR resolves issue [[#4841](https://github.com/psf/black/issues/4841)](https://github.com/psf/black/issues/4841), where Black 25.11.0 crashes or produces unstable formatting when `# fmt: off` and `# fmt: on` appear inside blocks of comments.

#### 🔧 Changes made:
- **BracketTracker.mark**: Ensures `bracket_depth` is set on all leaves, even when matching opening brackets are missing on the same line. Prevents `AttributeError` in `is_line_short_enough` when processing lines with only closing brackets.
- **Comment handling**: Updated `src/black/comments.py` and `src/black/linegen.py` to use `_contains_fmt_directive` instead of strict `in` checks. This correctly identifies nested or complex comment blocks (e.g., `# # fmt: off`) as `STANDALONE_COMMENT` blocks, avoiding incorrect splitting or unstable formatting.
- **Regression tests**: Added in `tests/test_fmt_off_on_comments.py` to ensure stability and prevent future regressions.

#### 📋 Why this matters:
- Fixes a regression introduced in commit `b895a73` related to `fmt` pragmas.
- Prevents internal errors and ensures consistent formatting behavior across versions.
- Improves robustness when handling real-world codebases with complex comment structures.
